newsitem.title: THAILAND: Siam Cement to face tougher second half.
newsitem.headline: Siam Cement to face tougher second half.

text.p: Thailand's largest industrial group Siam Cement Plc, hit by a huge foreign exchange loss from the de facto baht devaluation, faces a tough business outlook this year, analysts said on Friday.
"The second half will be tougher for the group. The demand has been so weak with very slow construction activities," said investment analyst Eric Henderson of ING Baring.

Thailand's severely sluggish economy and a tightening in government and private sector spending have depressed construction activities and cut demand for the group's cement and building materials, Henderson said.
The government plans to trim spending for 1997/98 (October- September) by up to 75 billion baht ($2.4 billion) to help balance its budget.
The budget cut is part of an International Monetary Fund- recommended $12-15 billion austerity programme to help Thailand revive its battered economy.
Siam Cement, Thailand's largest cement producer, is expected to post a big second-quarter loss when it reports earnings for the April-June period. The announcement is scheduled for August 27.
"This will be the first time in decades that Siam Cement will post a net loss," said an analyst at a U.S. investment bank.
Siam Cement announced last month a huge foreign exchange loss from its unhedged $4 billion foreign currency debts after the baht's sharp depreciation.
Thailand on July 2 replaced its long standing practice of pegging the baht to a dollar-dominated basket of currencies with a managed float regime. The baht has since lost more than 20 percent.
Siam Cement's shares have ended on Friday down six baht at 502, against a 788 baht finish on January 2 and 976 a year ago.
The company has said it has taken steps to ease foreign exchange risks by borrowing in different currencies that reflected the central bank's basket of currencies.
The group projected that it would incur up to a 9.9- billion-baht ($319.4-million) net loss if the baht eased to 30.00 to the dollar.
It said with every further one baht/dollar loss, it would face an additional 2.4 billion baht foreign exchange loss.
The baht traded at 31.130/31.230 per dollar in the domestic market and 30.75/30.85 offshore late on Friday.
Siam Cement said its foreign exchange loss would be fully booked on its second quarter financial statement.

Merrill Lynch said in a recent report that the baht's weakness would ultimately have a positive impact on Siam Cement as the higher prices of imported products boost its competitiveness and pressure smaller local competitors.
"Although the overall demand in the economy could shrink, Siam Cement's revenue should hold up as it survives and gains market share," Merrill Lynch said.
